name: Antti Herlin
current_role: Chairman of the Board, KONE Corporation (Helsinki)
profile: Finland's richest person and fourth-generation controlling owner of elevator/escalator maker KONE, which his great-grandfather invested in in 1924. He was KONE CEO 1996-2006 and has chaired the board since 2003. In April 2026 KONE agreed to combine with TK Elevator; Herlin is to remain chairman with over 50% of KONE's voting rights.
interesting_fact: KONE tests its elevators underground: in 2017 it expanded its Tytyri test facility to 350 m (1,150 ft) deep inside a working limestone mine in Lohja, Finland.
deep_cut_fact: Herlin owns a farm in Kirkkonummi, his birthplace west of Helsinki, where he raises Hereford and Aberdeen Angus beef cattle.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is KONE Global Head of Media Relations (Gia Forsman-Härkönen). KONE-TKE combination announced Apr 2026 (https://www.tkelevator.com/global-en/newsroom/press-releases/kone-and-tke-to-combine-creating-a-world-class-company-in-the-elevator-and-escalator-industry-197696.html) is a timely hook.

name: Sergey Katsiev
current_role: Co-owner and board member (former president, until 2015), Megapolis tobacco/FMCG distribution group, Russia
profile: Russian businessman who founded tobacco distributor Megapolis in 1998 after running Igor Kesaev's Mercury Tobacco Corporation from 1993; the two firms merged in 2006 and Megapolis became Russia's largest tobacco distributor (Philip Morris and JTI each took 20% in 2013). He stepped down as president in 2015 but remains a shareholder; in 2022 he and partners bought Imperial Brands' Russian assets.
interesting_fact: In 2022 Katsiev and his partners bought the Russian business of British tobacco company Imperial Brands as Western firms exited Russia.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering business he studied at the Moscow Institute of International Relations (MGIMO) and, after the Soviet collapse, worked at a Russian government trade mission in the Netherlands.
notes: Extremely private; did not answer calls from Kommersant even when he stepped down (https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/2714727). No published personal or press contact found; Megapolis is part of Igor Kesaev's Mercury group. Russia-based tobacco business - consider sanctions/reputational context before outreach.

name: Abigail (Abigail P. Johnson)
profile: Listed only as 'Abigail' sharing a 1997 Forbes entry with Edward C. (Ned) Johnson; this is almost certainly Abigail Johnson, Ned's daughter. She joined Fidelity full-time as an analyst in 1988 (after Hobart and William Smith and Harvard MBA), became CEO in 2014 and chairman in 2016, and runs the privately held, family-controlled asset manager today.

name: Jean Coutu
current_role: Founder, The Jean Coutu Group (now part of Metro Inc.); co-founder, Marcelle and Jean Coutu Foundation
profile: Montreal pharmacist (born 1927) who opened a discount pharmacy with partner Louis Michaud in 1969 and built The Jean Coutu Group into Quebec's dominant drugstore chain via franchising and acquisitions, including a large US arm. The family sold the company to Metro in 2017-18 for about C$4.5bn; he now focuses on philanthropy through the family foundation.
interesting_fact: His 1969 store pioneered the 'pharm-escompte' format in Quebec: low prices, broad non-pharmacy merchandise and long opening hours, which became the template for the franchise network launched in 1973.
deep_cut_fact: The first Pharm-Escompte Jean Coutu opened in June 1969 on avenue du Mont-Royal at the corner of rue Garnier in Montreal's Plateau; he reportedly put his life savings of about C$250,000 into it.
notes: Aged ~99; alive per latest available sources (no death report found as of Nov 2026, but verify before outreach). Not active in business; family foundation (fmjc.org, Montreal, supports Quebec causes and projects in Mali and Haiti) is the most plausible route. Life-savings figure from encyclopedia.com company history.

name: Luca Ferrari
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Bending Spoons S.p.A. (Milan; Nasdaq: BSP)
profile: Italian engineer who co-founded Bending Spoons in 2013 with Matteo Danieli, Francesco Patarnello and Luca Querella after their diary app Evertale failed. The Milan firm buys and overhauls tech products (Evernote, WeTransfer, Meetup, Eventbrite, Vimeo, AOL) and listed on Nasdaq on 1 July 2026 at $29/share; he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: The company name comes from the spoon-bending scene in The Matrix, which the founders tie to seeing problems from a completely different point of view.
deep_cut_fact: The four founders, University of Padua-trained engineers, met in Copenhagen on a dual-degree programme at the Technical University of Denmark; Bending Spoons was started with the roughly $40,000 left after winding up Evertale.
notes: Does long-form podcasts (20VC Mar 2024, All-In), so receptive to podcast format. Recently IPO'd (Jul 2026), so quiet-period/earnings timing may matter.

name: Yu Zhuyun
current_role: Chairman, Central New Energy Holding Group (HKEX: 1735) and Anhui Central Holding Group
profile: Zhejiang-born former soldier who worked at Comba Telecom in Hong Kong, sold his shares after Comba's 2003 IPO and founded Central Holding Group in Anhui in 2004. The group spans construction, real estate, logistics, wellness and, increasingly, solar module manufacturing, PV EPC, energy management and hydrogen/ammonia/methanol; he owns ~68% of HK-listed Central New Energy.
interesting_fact: His fortune was seeded by telecom, not property: he sold his stake in Comba Telecom after its 2003 Hong Kong listing and used the capital to start Central Holding Group in March 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Born in a village in Quzhou, Zhejiang, he served four years as a soldier in Anhui in the late 1980s and later returned to Anhui to found his group; in 2018 he committed 5 billion yuan to a healthcare and nursing complex in Qujiang district of his hometown.
notes: Strong energy angle (PV, hydrogen-ammonia-methanol). Low English-language profile; outreach likely needs Chinese. Contacts are listed-company secretary channels.

name: Alfred Gantner
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Partners Group (Baar-Zug, Switzerland); Chairman, Breitling SA (since Dec 2022)
profile: Swiss private-equity investor ('Fredy') who co-founded Partners Group in 1996 at age 28 with Goldman Sachs colleagues Marcel Erni and Urs Wietlisbach; he was CEO to 2005 and chairman 2005-2014. The firm listed in 2006 and manages $150bn+; he holds ~5%, chairs the founders' multi-family office PG3 and chairs Partners Group-owned watchmaker Breitling.

deep_cut_fact: He started out with a banking apprenticeship at Cantrade Privatbank (a former UBS subsidiary) before his BYU MBA, and in 2002 helped with Swiss public relations for the Salt Lake City Winter Olympics.

name: Cecilia Morel
current_role: Former First Lady of Chile (2010-14, 2018-22); heir to the Piñera family fortune (family investment group Bancard)
profile: Cecilia Morel Montes is the widow of former Chilean president and billionaire investor Sebastián Piñera (d. 2024), whose fortune came from introducing credit cards to Chile and stakes including LATAM Airlines; Hurun lists her as holder of the family wealth.
